page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1.2xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz. It features 8 dedicated physical cores with 1 thread per core, providing a total of 8 vCPUs. The instance is configured with 64.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it operates on a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates that the CPU performance of this instance is generally modest. Single-core and multi-core stress-ng tests place the processor in the bottom 25% of tested hardware, a trend mirrored by its Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores. However, the instance demonstrates average performance in large-block memory bandwidth tests, both for read and write operations, as well as in Passmark CPU and physics tests. Redis SET operations also achieve average throughput, reaching 5.94 million operations per second.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.se1.2xlarge is its lower computational speed and weak single-threaded compression performance, as evidenced by poor gzip and bzip3 decompression results. This makes it less suitable for compute-heavy or highly sequential processing tasks. However, the generous memory allocation of 8 GB per core provides qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads that do not require high-performance compute, such as caching layers, moderate database operations, and light web serving.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1.2xlarge is an x86_64 memory-optimized server instance featuring 8 dedicated Intel Xeon 8163 vCPUs running at 2.5 GHz and 64.0 GB of RAM. Lacking local storage and GPU accelerators, it relies on network-attached storage and offers a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. Performance benchmarks indicate modest CPU capabilities, with stress-ng and Geekbench scores falling into the bottom 25%. However, the instance maintains average performance in large-block memory bandwidth and Redis SET operations, processing 5.94 million operations per second. The high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core makes this instance qualitatively cost-effective for memory-intensive but compute-light workloads. It is best suited for caching layers, in-memory databases, and moderate web serving applications that require significant memory capacity without demanding high-frequency processing power.
